newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Thursday on institutional support at high levels, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 20.01 percent from 22 percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover rose sharply to 10.37 million lots from 5.08 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Rises in the Shanghai A share market were the major factors keeping rates at high levels today," one trader said.
Another factor supporting early-maturing contracts above the 20-percent level was fund demand by financial institutions ahead of the year-end, traders said.
"The year-end settlement has made financial institutions demand more funds recently," one trader added.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down because of reports the Finance Ministry will issue about 250 billion yuan in treasury bills next year, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 116.24 yuan from 115.87 yuan on Wednesday, with turnover rising to 860 million yuan from 540 million.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market rose to 1.53 million lots from 1.18 million.
"The contracts went down because of reports that the government would issue about 250 billion yuan in T-bills in 1997," one local trader said.
The 10-year bond bucked the trend and rose because of its comparatively higher coupon, traders said.
